text:
maya: FYI — getting spikes of Pending pods in gpu-prod nodepool. Autoscaler attempts a scale-up but the compute API returns quota errors for us-east1-b. (1723456789)
liam: which instance type and nodepool?
maya: a2-highgpu-1g, nodepool-gpu-prod. Logs show "quotaExceeded" then long retry loop.
andre: also seeing kube-scheduler backpressure: some pods never bind because PVC attach is queued behind other ops. Might be regional attach saturation.
chloe: can we failover to another cluster/region? latency to primary DB might go up for some customers.
ravi: quick idea: bring up a small standby nodepool in us-east1-c under a different GCP quota project (standby-project) with fast-attach flag and attach-policy: Immediate. Use smaller instance + MIG with GPU attach script to avoid long image pulls.
liam: cost tradeoff: smaller instances with fast attach cost ~1.4x/hr but avoid 5-10min waits + preempted requeues. need approval for short-term burn.
maya: preference: keep traffic in-region if possible. Cross-region increases KV cache miss and can push latency >200ms for some low-latency endpoints.
andre: technical constraints: PV attach/detach ops are zonal. Cross-zone pod rescheduling within same region is fine, but cross-region requires moving data or fallback to read-only caches.
chloe: can we use PodTopologySpread + nodeAffinity to prefer us-east1-a/b but allow fallback to c when capacity low?
ravi: yes — we can add a fallback priority class and toleration + anti-affinity flip. Autoscaler policy: enforce `scaleUpDelay: 15s` and `maxNodeCreationRate: 2` so we don't spam API. Also implement a preflight quota check before creating nodes.
liam: can you paste the error snippet?
maya: sure:
```
2024-04-05T10:11:34Z kube-controller-manager: error creating instance: compute.projects.zones.us-east1-b.instances.insert: quotaExceeded
Caused by: Quota 'GPUS_ALL_REGIONS' exceeded for project 12345.
```
andre: looks like project-level GPU quota across regions, not only zone. Standby-project trick works if it has spare quota.
chloe: what's the orchestration to flip active workloads? manual cordon/evict or automated?
ravi: propose automated policy:
- detect `Pending` > 10 for >= 60s and `quotaExceeded` in recent API errors
- spin up N=1 standby node in fallback zone under standby-project
- label nodes `fallback=true` and add nodeSelector to non-critical workloads via Admission webhook
- evict lower-priority pods (batch, rebuilds) onto fallback nodes first
- once healthy, promote by reducing affinity for some latency-tolerant requests
(We keep critical real-time routes pinned to primary pool)
liam: need rollback plan: if standby-project also runs out, revert scheduling and queue requests with backpressure. Also ensure we don't evict stateful pods without safe drains.
maya: and add an alert: P1 if eviction would affect >5% of latency-sensitive pods. Otherwise P2 for capacity.
sre-bot: alert created: GPUQuotaHigh_us-east1 (P2) — current usage 92% in us-east1 (1723456802)
andre: one more gotcha: image pull and node init time dominates. Use pre-baked node image with model artifacts or use init containers to pull models to a shared local disk on node startup. Fast-attach helps but doesn't help image pull.
ravi: plan for next 24h: (1) provision standby-project quota request, (2) create small standby nodepool template with baked images, (3) test autoscaler preflight + webhook in staging. I'll own the patches.
chloe: I'll run perf sims on the DB latency delta for cross-zone vs cross-region for the top 10 routes.
liam: finance note: finance OK with ephemeral spend up to $8k/day for emergency runway; add tags so we can attribute.
maya: assigning: ravi => infra runbook + patch, andre => bake node image, chloe => perf sims, liam => cost monitoring dashboard + tagging. I'll coordinate comms. :thumbsup:
ravi: starting a playbook draft in #runbooks and will attach links when ready.
maya: thanks — keep updates here, escalate to oncall if standby fails to come up.
